name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Saturday 5 July 1986

clue.text: Satisfactory rise in foreign currency?

blocks.note: first meaning: good enough, reaching the required standard
second, playful meaning: climbing as high as the German mark, a foreign currency in 1986

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading: something that rises until it reaches the level of the Deutschmark has gone up to the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means adequate or meeting the expected standard, as in work that is up to scratch.

clue.text: Fruit for 24, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak points at the spoken form of a word rather than its spelling

blocks.note: the answer at 24 across, a set of two, said out loud

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asks what fruit goes with another answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a common orchard fruit.

clue.text: The way a duck takes up grain

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking up lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ST is short for street, a way
taken as written
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: How a duck gobbles up seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is the bird in the surface; in cricket a duck is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal crop, so they are a kind of grain.

clue.text: The difficulty about one exalting a goddess

indicators.note: difficulty suggests trouble, so the word before it is thrown into disorder
exalting raises up, and in a down clue that means reading from the bottom
about means around, so the rearranged article wraps the other part

blocks.note: taken as written
an ace is a one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: The trouble with someone who praises a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: Difficulty reads as a noun with The, but it is the anagram signal for The alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft, crossroads and the night.

clue.text: Learned lady, contralto and queen run away in opera

blocks.note: a Master of Arts is a learned degree
a dame is a lady
Dame Clara Butt was a celebrated English contralto
ER, Elizabeth Regina
to fly is to flee

explanation.surface: A scholarly woman, a low-voiced singer and a queen all flee during an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Learned lady looks like one unit meaning a bluestocking, but it splits into a degree and a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame Butterfly is Puccini's 1904 opera about a Japanese geisha.

clue.text: American writer who up set a union — that one

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means placed upwards, so the letters read from the bottom

blocks.note: the NUR was Britain's National Union of Railwaymen
yon is an old word for that

explanation.surface: An American author who overturned a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: Up set is not upset, upsetting, but two words: the union's initials are set upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon Runyon was an American author of Broadway stories such as those behind Guys and Dolls.

clue.text: Show new set to Mr Dean

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so the following letters are made into a different order

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh television show is handed to a presenter called Dean.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate is to show how something works or prove it.

clue.text: Apportion food, say?

indicators.note: say asks us to take the word as spoken rather than as written

blocks.note: meat is food, and it is pronounced the same as the verb meaning to allot

explanation.surface: Someone is dividing up rations at a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to hand out or distribute shares, which is what apportioning does.

clue.text: Double lives?

blocks.note: surface reading: the secret second life of a spy or bigamist
setter's reading: double means more than one, so this is just the plural of a life lived

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests deception, but the setter only means lives in the plural, the ordinary sense of being alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A life is an existence, so more than one life are existences.

clue.text: Prior appears before church to tend injured

indicators.note: something injured is damaged out of its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Latin word for before, familiar from ante-room
CE is the Church of England
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior monk goes ahead of the congregation to nurse the wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: Prior looks like a monastic title in the surface, but it is the adjective meaning earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something antecedent comes earlier in time or order, so it is prior to what follows.

clue.text: Some invigorating port?

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following word is taken, a run of its letters

blocks.note: the second to fifth letters of this word

explanation.surface: A glass of fortified wine as a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Port reads as the drink in the surface; it is a seaport. Vigo is a fishing port in north-west Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigo is a major Atlantic seaport in Galicia, Spain, so it is an example of a port.

clue.text: Golf clubs carry measure for presenting booby prize

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so the clubs hold the measure between them

blocks.note: two golf clubs: a wood, and a spoon, an old name for a lofted wooden club
an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A golf club hands over a joke trophy to its worst player.
explanation.walkthrough: A wooden spoon is the mock prize given in Britain to whoever comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden spoon is the traditional mock award for finishing last, so it is a booby prize.

clue.text: Putting on a coat and disappearing? That's about right

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the single letter

blocks.note: vanishing means disappearing
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone puts on their coat and slips away, which seems fair enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The coat is a layer of finish on wood, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnishing a surface means applying a coat of glossy protective finish to it.

clue.text: Time of strain?

blocks.note: surface reading: a period of stress or tension
setter's reading: a strain is a passage of music, and its time is the speed at which it is played

explanation.walkthrough: Strain suggests pressure, but in music a strain is a melody, and the musical word for time or pace is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the speed of a piece is its tempo, often called its time.

clue.text: A negro wandering in the shade

indicators.note: wandering means roaming about, so these letters stray from their order

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man walking about in the shadow, in a dated phrasing typical of its 1986 date.
explanation.walkthrough: Shade looks like shadow, but here it means a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange is a colour, and a shade is a particular colour or hue.

clue.text: Stupid things, but capital savers

blocks.note: first meaning: silly people, as in calling someone a silly goose
second meaning: the sacred birds whose cackling warned Rome of the Gauls attacking the Capitol

explanation.walkthrough: Capital savers suggests thrifty investors; it refers to the legend that geese saved the Capitol in Rome around 390 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Goose is a word for a foolish person, and Livy tells how the Capitol's geese raised the alarm.

clue.text: Directions about mount backed in France

definitions.note: a place in France: the answer is a French city

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the mountain's name is read from its end
about means surrounding, so the compass points go around the other part

blocks.note: north and south, two compass directions
Mount Etna, the volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: Instructions for getting a horse to back up, given somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Mount suggests climbing on a horse; it is the volcano. The definition is the brief phrase saying where the place is.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a city on the Loire in western France, so it is a place found in France.

clue.text: A number order brick

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500
the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A numbered instruction for a builder to order bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Adobe is a sun-dried mud brick, so it is a type of brick.

clue.text: Play taken on road making a smash hit?

definitions.text: taken on road making a smash hit?

blocks.note: first meaning: a 1932 drama by J. B. Priestley

blocks.clueFragment: taken on road making a smash hit?
blocks.note: second meaning: a bend which, taken badly by a driver, causes a crash

explanation.walkthrough: Smash hit sounds like theatrical success, which fits the touring play of the surface, but the smash is a car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Priestley's well-known play has this title, and the phrase also names a hazardous bend on a road where accidents happen.

clue.text: Late president gives reasons for reform, leaving nothing out

indicators.note: leaving out means omitting, so the letter standing for nothing is dropped
to reform is to reshape, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A former head of state explains why change is needed, omitting nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Gamal Abdel Nasser was President of Egypt until his death in 1970.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasser led Egypt as president and had died long before 1986, so he is a late president.

clue.text: Perhaps quote Pater novel about the East

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters take a new arrangement
about means around, so the shuffled letters surround the compass point

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Perhaps cite a passage from a novel by Walter Pater about the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Pater was a Victorian writer, which makes novel look like a noun; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote is to repeat someone's words, so quoting is one example of repeating.

clue.text: Becoming fairly good?

blocks.note: first meaning: seemly, proper, appropriate
second meaning: reasonably satisfactory, quite good

explanation.walkthrough: Becoming looks like the verb turning into, but it is the adjective meaning suitable or seemly.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent behaviour is proper and seemly, and a decent meal is pretty good without being excellent.

clue.text: Hardy ruler?

blocks.note: surface reading: a tough, robust monarch
setter's reading: the novelist Thomas Hardy, whose Napoleonic verse epic is titled after a kind of hereditary ruler

explanation.walkthrough: Hardy looks like the adjective meaning tough, but it is the novelist Thomas Hardy, whose Napoleonic epic is named after a kind of ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynast is a hereditary ruler or member of a dynasty, the figures of Hardy's The Dynasts.

clue.text: TV comic in the paper?

definitions.note: the word found in the name of an abrasive paper

blocks.note: first meaning: Dick ..., a British television comedian of the 1960s and 70s
second meaning: the grit coating a sanding sheet, as in the name of that paper

explanation.walkthrough: In the paper suggests a cartoon in a newspaper, but the paper is sandpaper of a particular kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery is the abrasive mineral coating emery paper, and Dick Emery was a popular British TV comedian.

clue.text: One in standard two

indicators.note: in places one element inside the other, as a filling sits within its case

blocks.note: par is the normal standard, as in golf
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pupil in the second year of school.
explanation.walkthrough: Standard two reads like a school class; standard is the word that holds the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a set of two things, so it can stand for the number.

clue.text: Making fighter duck?

blocks.note: first meaning: the Mitsubishi ..., a Japanese fighter plane of the Second World War
second meaning: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing

explanation.walkthrough: The opening word Making sits oddly; read the clue as a fighter making a duck, the plane's name and the cricket score being the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zero was a famous wartime fighter aircraft, and a batsman's duck is a score of nought.

clue.text: Tennis ace has bungled point

indicators.note: bungled means messed up, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a point of the compass, East

explanation.surface: A top tennis player has fluffed an important point.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe was an American tennis champion who won Wimbledon in 1975.

clue.text: Yeomen with something of the lower type in them?

definitions.text: Yeomen with something of the lower type in them?

blocks.clueFragment: Yeomen with something of the lower type in them?
blocks.note: surface reading: guardsmen with a coarse or lower-class streak
setter's reading: a lower is something that lows, a cow, and these men have eaten its meat

explanation.walkthrough: Lower reads as the comparative of low, but it is the noun for an animal that moos. The Yeomen Warders at the Tower of London have a well-known nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yeomen Warders of the Tower of London are popularly called by this name, said to come from their beef rations.

clue.text: Girl in Russian river lost head

indicators.note: losing its head means the river's name gives up its opening letter

blocks.note: the longest river in Europe, flowing through Russia

explanation.surface: A young woman in a Russian river is swept under and drowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Olga is a girl's name, especially common in Russia, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Untravelled people love amethysts — a peculiar eccentricity

indicators.note: something peculiar and eccentric is odd and off-centre, so the letters before it are jumbled

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: People who never travel have an odd fondness for purple gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Stay-at-homes are people who prefer not to go anywhere, so they are untravelled.
